string.text: Intelligence is the chance that a stalker makes the right decision in a fight. It grows with his Rank, and even a legend sometimes gets it wrong. Personality is how his faction fights, after the character types GSC designed for the Zone. Some factions hold their ground, others press or run, and two stalkers of the same faction can still fight differently.
This sets the chance that a novice makes the right decision, and each higher rank adds to it. The chance stops at 75 percent, whatever the Rank.
Each rank above novice adds this much to the chance of the right decision.

Push and Pull act on weak moments in a fight, against you or another stalker. Push presses an enemy who cannot answer, and Pull draws a stalker back while he is the weak one. Each ends when the moment passes.
Attackers fire longer bursts at a target who cannot answer, and move to closer cover when he bleeds or turns his back. (Intelligence, Personality)
Push on reload and empty mag
The push starts when his target reloads or runs empty, and ends when the weapon is back up.
Healthy attackers close in on a badly hurt target to finish the fight, until he recovers.
A stalker who is reloading, or hurt after a hit, falls back to farther cover while his enemy is strong, and the pull ends when he recovers. (Intelligence, Personality)

Commitment keeps a stalker on a fire action, at the same cover, while it still works. He switches as soon as he loses sight, his shot is blocked or his enemy is gone. Inactive on modded exes without this feature.

Conduct gives disciplined stalkers better habits in how they hold cover and how close they fight. A stalker has the discipline for life or not at all, and trained military factions have it most often. Inactive on modded exes without this feature.
An experienced rifleman or sniper crouches to fire when the crouched line to his enemy is clear, and stands to fire over low cover that blocks it. (Intelligence, Personality)
A disciplined stalker picks cover that suits his weapon, closer with a submachine gun, and farther with a sniper rifle as his rank rises. (Intelligence, Personality)

Reaction gives each rank a different aim, in how fast the barrel follows a moving target, how tightly it holds a strafing one, and how well he leads a runner. Inactive on modded exes without this feature.
Discipline gives each rank a different trigger, and higher ranks fire shorter bursts more often. Inactive on modded exes without this feature.
Planned: stalkers answer and open fire as far as their weapon reaches. Today a stalker shot from beyond the fight range can only take cover. There is no setting yet.
Planned: player-facing combat feedback, concussion first. Nothing to configure yet.

Intelligence is the chance that a mutant makes the right move in a fight. It grows with the Map level, from Cordon up to Jupiter and Pripyat, but even there a mutant sometimes makes the wrong move. Personality is the set of moves a mutant carries, after the species GSC designed. Two chimeras of a pack can still fight differently. Wild is how far the numbers of a species vary between individuals, like the force of a leap. A mutant waits between its moves. If one of those moves hits you, no mutant starts another on you for a moment. This is why a pack comes at you in turns.

A mutant's toughness, scaled by the map rank (rookie maps rank 0 up to endgame maps rank 5): damage resistance grows by the slider's percent per rank. Multiplies the installed balance, so other mutant overhauls keep their numbers.
Personality decides which of these moves a mutant carries, and Intelligence decides when to take one.

The creature keeps using these attacks as the game made it. On top of that, Intelligence picks the right moment, like a gravity throw while you reload or a cloak when you take aim. Personality decides whether a mutant uses them that way at all.
These abilities work as the game made them. Wild spreads their numbers between individuals. At 0 they keep the game's values.
This sets the chance that a mutant in Cordon and the Swamps makes the right move, and each higher Map level adds to it. The chance stops at 75 percent, whatever the Map level.
Each Map level above Cordon adds this much to the chance of the right move.
A higher value spreads the numbers of a species wider between individuals, like the force of a leap and the reach of a gravity throw. At 0 all mutants of a species have the same numbers.
Hit power grows by this percent for each map rank: rank 0 stays vanilla, rank 5 gets 5 times this bonus.
Damage a mutant receives shrinks by this percent for each map rank, so a deep-Zone mutant shrugs off fire a Cordon one would feel.

Jumps up at an enemy standing higher than the mutant, like on a rock, even at close range. All species but the chimera and the lurker wind up first, which gives you time to react. (Intelligence, Personality, Wild)
Springs at once at an enemy aiming at the mutant, and at one with no way to fire back, like while you reload, sprint or turn away. (Intelligence, Personality, Wild)
Goes for a moving enemy, then steers toward him in the air. All species but the chimera and the lurker wind up first. (Intelligence, Personality, Wild)
Goes for a moving enemy with no wind-up, then steers toward him in the air. (Intelligence, Personality, Wild)

Aims at the spot where a moving enemy will be when the mutant comes down, with no steering in the air. All species but the chimera and the lurker wind up first. A smarter mutant leads its target more. (Intelligence, Personality, Wild)
Aims with no wind-up at the spot where a moving enemy will be when the mutant comes down, with no steering in the air. A smarter mutant leads its target more. (Intelligence, Personality, Wild)

Closes the distance to an enemy on a perch, and to you if you aim at the bloodsucker from mid range. The jump itself does no damage, but the claws strike once the bloodsucker lands. (Intelligence, Personality, Wild)
Turns and strikes at an enemy beside or behind the mutant up close. (Intelligence, Personality)
Strikes at point blank with no wind-up, if the chimera or the lurker faces its enemy up close. (Intelligence, Personality)
Throws when you look away from the burer, and also when you have no way to fire back, like while you reload. This is when the burer has no need for its shield. (Intelligence, Personality)
Spreads how often a burer throws its gravity attack, and the range, speed and radius of the throw. (Wild)
Spreads how many objects a burer lifts, how far away it finds them, the range it throws them from and how fast the objects fly. (Wild)
Spreads how long a controller must see you before its psy attack, and the pause between two attacks. (Wild)
Spreads how much stamina a blow from the controller takes from you. (Wild)
Spreads the strength and reach of the controller's auras. (Wild)
Spreads how far away a poltergeist senses you, how fast your movement gives you away, and how quickly it loses you again. (Wild)
The bloodsucker vanishes for a short time if you aim at it or hit it, then shows again. Once close enough to strike, the bloodsucker attacks instead. (Intelligence, Personality)
A badly hurt mutant runs from the fight for a while if its enemy is not close and the mutant is not facing him. A mutant with a lower Intelligence flees more often. (Intelligence, Personality, Wild)
Healing lets wounded stalkers use the medkits and bandages they carry, and you can see it, as a hurt man limps and a healing one plays the gesture.
Adds the heal rate, the healing charge by rank, and a pause in healing while he fights. The item lists stay restored with it off.
Scales how much health each heal restores. 2.0 heals twice as fast, and 0.5 half as fast.
The chance a novice carries a healing charge, used when he is hurt with no medkit left. 50 percent is the game's value for every rank.
The same chance for an experienced stalker.
The same chance for a veteran.
The same chance for a master.
A hurt stalker near you limps while out of combat, standing or walking, matched to the weapon he carries. A fight ends the limp.
The health below which a stalker limps. Lower values wait until he is more badly hurt.
A stalker near you plays a medkit or bandage gesture when he starts to heal, out of combat only.
Accuracy gives each rank a different spread, tight for a legend and wide for a novice. Moving fire adds a second curve, and a higher rank keeps a steadier aim while he walks or runs.
Each rank fires with a different spread, wide for a novice and tight for a legend. (Rank)
Higher ranks keep their aim while they fire on the move. (Rank)
Spread for a novice, as a multiple of vanilla. Lower is tighter, and 1.00 is vanilla.
Each rank above novice changes the spread by this much. Negative values tighten it as rank rises.
Spread for a novice while he walks or runs, as a multiple of vanilla. 1.00 is vanilla, and lower is steadier.
Each rank above novice changes his spread on the move by this much. Negative values steady his fire as rank rises.
Higher ranks follow a moving target faster and hold a strafing target longer. (Rank)
How fast a novice's barrel follows a moving target once it is close, in radians per second. 0.24 is vanilla.
Each rank above novice adds this much speed.
How tightly a novice holds a strafing target, as the width of the lock band in radians. 0.196 is vanilla, where a strafing target moves out of his aim.
Each rank above novice widens the band by this much, and higher ranks hold a strafing target longer.
A stalker aims ahead of a moving target by the round's real flight time, and higher ranks lead more truly. (Rank)
How far ahead a novice aims, as a multiple of the correct lead. 2.00 aims twice too far ahead, and 1.00 is exact.
Each rank above novice changes the lead by this much. Negative values bring it toward 1.00 as rank rises.
Higher ranks confirm a threat they glimpse sooner, and a novice stays at the speed of your install. (Rank)
Higher ranks fire shorter bursts more often. (Rank)
Burst length for a novice, as a multiple of vanilla. Below 1.00 shortens the burst.
Each rank above novice changes the burst length by this much. Keep it at or above the cadence value, or the rate of fire drops.
The pause between a novice's bursts, as a multiple of vanilla. Below 1.00 fires more often.
Each rank above novice changes the pause by this much. Negative values shorten it as rank rises.
How fast a novice turns a glimpse into a confirmed threat, as a multiple of your install. 1.00 is the speed of your install.
Each rank above novice adds this much speed.
How far out a novice starts to notice a threat, as a multiple of your install. 1.00 is the range of your install.
Each rank above novice adds this much range.

A stalker firing with a clear shot keeps his cover, even when a better spot opens nearby. Losing sight, a blocked shot or an enemy out of range still lets him move. Inactive on modded exes without this feature.

When his enemy cannot answer, because he is reloading, empty, unarmed, sprinting, climbing or turned away, a stalker keeps firing past his commitment limit. He moves once the enemy can answer again, and mutants never trigger it. (Intelligence, Personality)
Applies to every stalker outside a maneuver.
The longest stretch a stalker holds an action, after which X-Ray may move him again. He still breaks off as soon as his reason to hold ends.

A maneuver is a complete takeover of a stalker for a real tactical move, like a counterflank, a pickoff or reload cover. The system is built for coordinated, military-style squad tactics, and many more maneuvers are coming. Intelligence decides whether he takes a move, and Personality whether he carries it at all.
Lets AlifeTactics take a stalker over for a maneuver in any fight near you, against you or another stalker. The other Combat pages have separate switches.
No maneuver takes a companion over, and a companion mutant is left alone too.
A stalker hit while standing, or staggered by the hit, holds his place until the reaction ends. It works on every stalker, in a maneuver or not. Inactive on modded exes without this feature.
A stalker fighting someone else turns on you and holds his ground when you come closer than his target. (Intelligence, Personality)

A stalker caught reloading in a watcher's line of fire runs to the nearest cover that hides him, reloading on the way. Unwatched, he reloads where he stands. Inactive on modded exes without this feature. (Intelligence, Personality)

A stalker whose enemy gets inside his weapon's minimum range backs away along a clear lane until he has room to use his weapon, still firing. For example, a sniper backs away from a man with a shotgun. (Intelligence, Personality)

A hurt stalker whose spot is exposed to a nearby enemy falls back to cover behind him, still firing. With no cover in reach he backs off along a clear lane, and two stalkers never take the same cover. (Intelligence, Personality)

A hurt stalker who is the last of his squad puts his weapon away and runs to a friendly base when nobody is shooting at him. A lower Intelligence makes him flee more often. (Intelligence, Personality)

A stalker who outranges his enemy in a standoff holds his position and fires single aimed shots. He stops when the enemy comes close enough to hit back, when he takes fire, or when the enemy has him in sight. (Intelligence, Personality)
Crossfire cuts the damage a stalker deals to stalkers he is not hostile to, and a crossfire between allies stops killing them. Your shots and fights between enemies stay at full damage.
Applies to hits between any stalkers who are not hostile to each other, across factions too.
The share of damage such a hit deals. 0.00 means no damage, and 1.00 is full vanilla damage.

Vision gives each rank a different detection, in how fast a stalker turns a glimpse into a confirmed threat and how far out he starts to notice one. A novice matches your install, and higher ranks notice sooner and farther. Inactive on modded exes without this feature.

Danger fixes how stalkers react to a threat they sense, on top of whichever danger scheme your modpack ships. It adds a reaction to distant hits and to a missed knife swing, and it sets how hard NPCs focus on you.

Sound lets hostile stalkers hear you before they see you. Your loud sounds reach the game's hearing, and your quieter steps and handling make them turn or walk over to check. Crouched movement is silent, and your stealth mods keep control of how you are seen.
A stalker hit from far off turns and seeks cover, even when the shot came from past his reaction range.

A stalker in front of you notices a knife swing that misses him within 3 m. He gets up, raises his weapon and faces you, and a hostile who then sees you fights. A neutral or friend reacts only while Neutral gunfire alert is on.

A neutral or friendly stalker reacts when your bullet strikes near him, a reaction the engine would otherwise drop. He does not turn hostile, and the same switch covers your missed knife swing at a neutral or friend.

Hostile stalkers hear you move. A walk carries 5 m, a sprint 1.6 times farther and a jump landing 10 m, and the surface and rain change the distance. A walk turns him weapon-ready toward the sound, and a sprint or a landing sends him walking over to check.
Hostile stalkers hear your reload within 8 m, an empty click within 6 m and an item use within 5 m. A reload or an empty click sends him walking over, and an item turns him weapon-ready toward you.
A standing stalker out of combat glances toward a creature he hears within 5 to 10 m, a mutant always and a stalker only when he is hostile. He turns his head and stays where he is.
Scales how far your movement and handling noise carries. Below 1.00 makes stealth more forgiving, and above 1.00 lets stalkers hear you from farther.

How strongly an NPC focuses on you while you can see him, against the pull other targets have. 300 weighs you like any other fighter, 900 is the vanilla pull toward you, and 0 removes it. Inactive on modded exes without this feature.

A ricochet, the sound of a fight nearby and an ally under attack each read the settings of another danger. Stalkers reacted to them at the wrong range and for the wrong time, but now each danger has the right settings.
A fresh mutant corpse ended a stalker's danger reaction early. Mutant corpses no longer interrupt it.
The danger check could crash the game for a stalker gone from the level a moment before. The check now leaves him alone.
If a danger had a broken time value, the danger check could crash the game. The check now skips any danger like that.
A stalker hit by a bullet lost track of the shooter. Now he turns to the shooter and takes cover from that direction.
If a stalker switched danger reactions, the animation of the old reaction could keep playing. The old animation now stops at each change.
If a stalker left the danger reaction, the claims of all stalkers to cover spots were wiped, and two of them could pick the same spot. Now he clears only the claim he made.
The game could crash when a corpse vanished while a stalker went to check it. He now stops.
If you were the killer, the corpse search could move the wrong squadmate. Now the finder of the body does the search.
At the end of a corpse search a stalker walked back to the old spot and left the cover he had found unused. He now goes to that cover.
The danger check read its settings again at each pass for each stalker, which cost time in a crowd. It now reads them once.
A new stalker taking over the id of a dead one also took over the last alarm. That alarm now clears with the dead stalker.
The game could crash when a corpse reaction ran before its search had started. It now waits.
These are the bugs in Anomaly and X-Ray that AlifeTactics fixes, grouped by the system they live in. All rows are locked. Most fixes always run, but some need the option named in their line.
A dead stalker kept running the danger reaction until the body vanished, and the log filled with an error. The reaction now stops at death.
After holding fire for a friend in the line of fire, a stalker kept walking weapon-ready once the fight ended. Now he returns to normal once the enemy is gone.

Stalkers held fire for any friend close by in any direction, and for one far behind the target. In a crowd the hold kept renewing, and the hold also silenced campers, helicopter fire and the finishing of wounded enemies. A stalker now holds and steps aside only if a friend stands between him and the target.

A stalker checked his line of fire for friends against the feet of a chimera or a burer, because neither creature has the spine bone the check looks for, and the log filled with an engine warning. He now checks it against the body.
A stalker attacked a second time turned to where the first attacker had stood, and only the first corpse he searched played the search animation. The memory of each danger now clears at its end.
A stalker dodges a grenade that lands near him and turns to face one that lands farther off. AlifeTactics now sets the distance that splits the two.
A stalker shot by an enemy he could not see kept firing at a target he could see. He now turns to the attacker, and that pull fades with distance. Inactive on modded exes without this feature.

Stalkers made you their target much more often if you saw them than if another stalker did, and whole groups picked you. The Perception > Danger > Player target pull slider sets how hard you pull. Inactive on modded exes without this feature.

All stalkers shot with the spread meant for the best shots, a novice included, because the game's rank scale stops far below the ranks Anomaly uses. Now each rank has a different spread. Works while Effectiveness > Accuracy > Enable Dispersion is on.

X-Ray crouches a stalker in a fight without checking that he can still hit his enemy from there, and he fired into the low cover in front of him. He now crouches only when the crouched line to his enemy is clear. Works while Combat > Conduct > Cover posture is on.

A standing stalker hit by a bullet slid across the ground while the hit animation played. Now he holds his place until the animation ends. Works while Combat > General > Hit reaction hold is on. Inactive on modded exes without this feature.
A maneuver could start on a stalker still staggering from a hit or playing a scripted animation. It now waits until the animation ends. Works while Combat > Maneuvers > Enable combat takeover is on.
Each load rolled a stalker's healing charge again, and stalkers that had used it could have it back. The charge is now rolled once for each stalker.

X-Ray stops a stalker's leg animation while a gesture plays. A stalker who bandaged on the move slid with frozen legs. The gesture now plays only while he stands still. Works while Mechanics > Healing > Healing animation is on.

The limp is a gesture too, and a limping stalker pulled into a fight kept the pose and slid when he was shot. He now drops the limp the moment a fight starts. Works while Mechanics > Healing > Limping animation is on.

X-Ray holds the whole body of a stalker in a gesture until it ends, and a stalker who started to heal near an enemy stood locked in place. The gesture now starts only while he has no enemy. Works while Mechanics > Healing > Healing animation is on.
A stalker shot from far off ignored the hit, because the shot came from past the reaction range. He now turns and takes cover. Works while Perception > Danger > Distant hits is on.

The check for a clear crouched shot started at chest height, above low cover that blocked the crouched line, and stalkers crouched into that cover. The check now starts at the height of a crouched stalker's eyes. Works while Combat > Conduct > Cover posture is on.
Monolith fighters flipped between a crouch and an idle stance for as long as the fight lasted. Their combat actions now count as combat, and they keep their stance.
Stalkers never used the medkits and bandages they carried, because the game's lists of those items were empty. The lists now name the vanilla items, and stalkers heal from what they carry.
A chimera or lurker could jump again the moment it landed, and put a second hit on you right after the first. Both now rest after each jump. Inactive on modded exes without this feature.
Jamming lets NPC weapons jam only from wear. In X-Ray every NPC also rolls an extra jam, and even a new rifle jams, with no jam animation to show it. Your weapon stays as it is.
NPC weapons jam only as their condition wears down.

Ammo lets veteran and higher stalkers fire the armor-piercing rounds they carry, and switch back to standard rounds when those run out. A fight may use up a carried box, sooner for quick-firing weapons and lower ranks. It works only while the game gives NPCs unlimited ammo.
Stalkers who carry armor-piercing rounds load them and use them up fight by fight.

Attachments let stalkers fit the scopes, silencers and grenade launchers they carry to their pistol or rifle, once they are out of a fight with their hands free. A scope then shows on the gun at the next quiet moment.
Stalkers fit attachments from their inventory at the next quiet moment. Story and named characters keep their guns as they are.

Gear lets the artefacts and equipment a stalker carries work for him, by the artefact's anomaly class. The strongest artefact on a channel counts and they do not stack, and a stalker with the air warping around him carries a real artefact.
An artefact gives its carrier up to 10 percent on its channel, and only the strongest counts.
Gravity artefacts and armor plates cut the damage their carrier takes.
Electric and quest artefacts raise the damage their carrier's shots deal.
Thermal artefacts tighten their carrier's aim.
Chemical artefacts give their carrier a slow health restore. Inactive on modded exes without this feature.
A stalker carrying any artefact warps the air around him, and you can tell he has one.
A stalker with binoculars sees farther by day. Inactive on modded exes without this feature.
A stalker with a night-vision device sees farther at night. Inactive on modded exes without this feature.

These are the tools for testing AlifeTactics and for reporting a bug. The log traces every system, the world trace records the fight around you, and the debug HUD shows what drives each fighter near you. Keep the log at Warn and the other two off in normal play, because tracing costs time.
Error writes failures only, Warn adds problems worth a look, Info adds the startup lines, and Debug traces every decision with its timing. The log is alifetactics.log, in the game's log folder.
Writes each line to disk the moment it is logged. Turn it on to chase a crash, and the last lines before it reach the file. It slows the game, and normal play needs it off.

Each fighter near you gets two lines. The first shows his name, health and the system driving him. The second shows his target with the distance, and the scheme and state X-Ray runs for him. The row colour names the driving system, and a mutant's move takes the colour of its group on the Mutants tab. The HUD refreshes twice a second and hides while the PDA is open.

Records the fight around you to alifetactics_world.log. It flags a body that slides, a shot fired far off the aim, two systems fighting over a stalker and a mutant that runs in place, and it writes a table of hits and bursts each minute. Each line names the system driving that fighter. Switched off, it stops recording and runs no checks.
Restores every AlifeTactics setting to its default. Use it after an update that changed the menu.
Warning: save or discard pending MCM changes first, otherwise they override the reset on the next Apply.
AlifeTactics: all settings restored to defaults.
